trajectory: fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki / Enhertu / DS-8201 / Daiichi Sankyo + AstraZeneca
refined_summary: Search discovery confirms a branching success trajectory rather than a single success flag. Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca announced a global development/commercialization collaboration in March 2019, with Daiichi retaining Japan rights. The first U.S. breast-cancer approval arrived in December 2019 under accelerated approval. DESTINY-Breast04 later tested a defined HER2-low population (IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-) and led to the August 2022 U.S. HER2-low breast-cancer approval. The current U.S. label retains a boxed warning for ILD/pneumonitis, demonstrating that safety trajectory is part of the asset state, not an annotation after success.
possible_primary_source_types: Daiichi Sankyo/AstraZeneca collaboration agreement announcements and filings
source_origin_notes: Daiichi and AstraZeneca releases about the same collaboration are one deal-origin cluster, not two independent confirmations.
ClinicalTrials.gov is sponsor-provided for design/history but useful for stable identifiers and dated record history.
FDA label/approval records are regulator-origin and should anchor indication/safety state.
